Site.faq1A: SciSpark is an AI workspace for academic research across disciplines. Discover scholarly papers, read with context, and build connected knowledge. It brings your paper feed, personal wiki, knowledge graph, and research ideas into one place, with Sparky as your research companion.
Site.faq2Q: How is the hosted version different from local?
Site.faq2A: The hosted beta runs in your browser and keeps your vault online. Local installation stores your Markdown vault on your computer. Both approaches may send requests to scholarly services and your chosen AI provider. Automatic sync between hosted and local vaults is not currently part of this offer.
Site.faq3Q: Do I need my own AI API key?
Site.faq3A: The hosted beta includes a starter AI allowance, and you can choose to connect your own API key. Local installation needs an API provider or a signed-in Codex or Claude Code CLI for AI features. Provider charges depend on the option you use.
Site.faq4A: SciSpark uses your research interests and profile to find academic papers from scholarly sources such as arXiv, OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar, and PubMed. In the preview above, choose one of three topics to see how discovery connects to reading, notes, and ideas. The preview is not a live recommendation feed.
Site.faq5A: A native mobile app is planned, so your research can be closer at hand. For now, you can open the hosted beta in your browser.
Site.closingBody: Discover with purpose. Read with context. Keep what you learn.
Site.footerLine: One workspace, from discovery to your next experiment.
Site.fallback: The interactive preview could not load. You can still explore SciSpark in the beta.

Topics.aiWhy: Connects your interest in language models with how information is represented and retrieved.
Topics.aiNote: Attention helps a model relate parts of an input. Retrieval brings external information into generation. Together, they open questions about context and evidence.
Topics.aiQuestion: When does retrieving a source help more than adding a longer context?
Topics.aiMethod: Compare the two approaches on the same questions, checking source attribution as well as answer quality.
Topics.climateWhy: Connects your interest in climate and energy with methods for modeling a changing atmosphere.
Topics.climateNote: Graph-based and transformer-based models offer different ways to represent weather. Comparing their assumptions can inform questions about forecasts and extreme events.
Topics.climateQuestion: How do learned weather models behave when the conditions become unusual?
Topics.climateMethod: Compare forecast errors across ordinary conditions and selected extremes, using the same regions, dates, and evaluation targets.
Topics.mindWhy: Connects your interest in learning and behavior with models of how people understand the world and other minds.
Topics.mindNote: Causal understanding and models of other agents offer complementary perspectives on learning. Observed behavior can inspire hypotheses, without establishing a model of human cognition.
Topics.mindQuestion: What kind of prior knowledge helps a learner infer another agent's goals?
Topics.mindMethod: Compare learners with different prior knowledge on the same observed behaviors, keeping computational results separate from claims about people.

Papers.attentionSummary: The Transformer uses attention to connect information across a sequence, without recurrent or convolutional layers. The paper evaluates the architecture on translation tasks.
Papers.ragTitle: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks
Papers.ragSummary: RAG combines a generative model with retrieved passages, bringing external sources into knowledge-intensive language tasks.
Papers.graphcastTitle: GraphCast: Learning skillful medium-range global weather forecasting
Papers.graphcastSummary: GraphCast learns from weather reanalysis data and uses a graph neural network to predict the evolution of atmospheric conditions.
Papers.panguTitle: Pangu-Weather: A 3D High-Resolution Model for Fast and Accurate Global Weather Forecast
Papers.panguSummary: Pangu-Weather uses a three-dimensional transformer and temporal aggregation to model global weather from historical atmospheric data.
Papers.learningTitle: Building Machines That Learn and Think Like People
Papers.learningSummary: This perspective connects cognitive science and machine learning, emphasizing causal models, compositionality, and learning from limited experience.
Papers.mindSummary: A neural network learns to predict agents' behavior from observations in simplified environments. The study explores computational models of other agents.
Papers.qwen3Summary: Qwen3 combines fast responses and extended reasoning in one model family, with a configurable thinking budget and multilingual training.
Papers.deepseekr1Title: DeepSeek-R1: Incentivizing Reasoning Capability in LLMs via Reinforcement Learning
Papers.deepseekr1Summary: The study explores reinforcement learning for language-model reasoning and transfers reasoning capabilities to smaller models through distillation.
Papers.s1Summary: A small curated training set and budget forcing let a language model spend more computation checking its answers on reasoning tasks.
Papers.deepseekv3Summary: This report describes a mixture-of-experts language model and the architecture and training choices used to improve computational efficiency.
Papers.olmo2Summary: OLMo 2 releases model weights, training data, code, and checkpoints, alongside techniques for more stable and efficient language-model training.
Papers.llama3Summary: The Llama 3 report documents a family of language models, covering pretraining, post-training, and evaluation across a range of language tasks.
Papers.regionalweatherTitle: Building Machine Learning Limited Area Models: Kilometer-Scale Weather Forecasting in Realistic Settings
Papers.regionalweatherSummary: Graph-based regional weather models incorporate boundary forecasts and are evaluated over Denmark and Switzerland using analyses and observations.
Papers.seasonalweatherTitle: Skilful global seasonal predictions from a machine learning weather model trained on reanalysis data
Papers.seasonalweatherSummary: ACE2 is tested on winter seasonal forecasts, with promising predictability and remaining limits for extreme conditions outside its training data.
Papers.efficientweatherTitle: Data-Efficient Ensemble Weather Forecasting with Diffusion Models
Papers.efficientweatherSummary: The authors compare training-data sampling strategies for diffusion forecasts, examining how temporal coverage can reduce data requirements.
Papers.auroraTitle: A Foundation Model for the Earth System
Papers.auroraSummary: Aurora learns from diverse Earth-system data and adapts to forecasting tasks including weather, air quality, waves, and cyclone tracks.
Papers.ace2Title: ACE2: Accurately learning subseasonal to decadal atmospheric variability and forced responses
Papers.ace2Summary: ACE2 emulates atmospheric variability from days to decades while conserving global dry air mass and moisture; some forcing responses remain imperfect.
Papers.continuousweatherTitle: Continuous Ensemble Weather Forecasting with Diffusion models
Papers.continuousweatherSummary: Continuous ensemble forecasting generates coherent weather trajectories in parallel, reducing reliance on repeated autoregressive forecast steps.
Papers.behaviorpredictionTitle: Context-Aware Human Behavior Prediction Using Multimodal Large Language Models: Challenges and Insights
Papers.behaviorpredictionSummary: A modular framework tests how visual context, prompts, and in-context examples affect language models' predictions of human activities.
Papers.cognitionaiTitle: Protecting Human Cognition in the Age of AI
Papers.cognitionaiSummary: This review examines how generative AI may influence thinking and learning, and discusses educational designs that encourage deeper cognitive engagement.
Papers.multihumanTitle: Seeing is Believing (and Predicting): Context-Aware Multi-Human Behavior Prediction with Vision Language Models
Papers.multihumanSummary: CAMP-VLM combines visual context and scene graphs to predict multiple people's activities, testing transfer from simulated to real-world sequences.
Papers.socialsimulationTitle: Social Simulations with Large Language Model Risk Utopian Illusion
Papers.socialsimulationSummary: The study finds that language-model social simulations can portray overly idealized behavior, highlighting biases to examine before drawing conclusions about people.
Papers.centaurTitle: Centaur: a foundation model of human cognition
Papers.centaurSummary: Centaur is fine-tuned on behavioral experiments to predict human choices, with evaluations on held-out participants and new task settings.
Papers.generativepeopleSummary: Interview-grounded agents are evaluated against participants' survey answers and behavior, studying how personal context affects behavioral simulation.
